correctness.rationale: The PMF normalizes by monotone survival. A direct three-term survival cross-product is affine in the tilt, yielding exact iff comparisons for every integer. Positivity follows from strict log concavity of the Erlang-2 survival. Cubic coefficients are independently reconstructed; Descartes signs prove exactly one threshold minimum, hence a single contiguous interval of decreasing hazard steps. The six decisive signs in the example are certified by rational bounds on exp(-1/2) from a 25th-order alternating series. Compact-uniform Taylor convergence and unique valley prove the fine-scale constant and level-crossing limits. Finite grids are only supporting diagnostics; the analytic argument covers all admissible parameters and ages. The package has executable source and no hidden file dependencies.

value.rationale: An exact if-and-only-if ageing boundary is natural for a published discrete reliability model whose source relies on visual hazard shapes. The cubic root plus two lattice candidates makes the infinite-support test finite; a non-reentrant descent theorem controls the whole shape, while the exact two-turn example and beta-scale asymptotic explain behavior otherwise missed by short plots. It informs reliability interpretation beyond a routine numerical fit or a mere renaming.
